title: Amid hardware legal battle, OpenAI releases a $230 keyboard for Codex
slides: Why would OpenAI sell a keyboard amid a legal war?
The $230 device is designed for Codex, not typing.
It has no keys—just pressure sensors for gestures.
Your next code sprint might skip the keyboard entirely.
Test a gesture-based workflow before your competitors do.
thread_text:
1. Why risk a keyboard?

OpenAI faces a lawsuit over a device that can't type a single letter.

2. No keys at all.

The $230 slab uses pressure sensors for gestures, not for typing text.

3. Built for code, not email.

Codex interprets your hand movements so you never touch a keyboard in a sprint.

4. Skip the keyboard entirely.

Your next code sprint might happen with just gestures and voice.

5. Test a gesture workflow today.

Open ChatGPT, try describing a function with only hand motions. Does it save time or add friction?

instagram.caption:
OpenAI is selling a $230 keyboard slab with no keys—just pressure sensors that read hand gestures for coding in Codex.

The device sidesteps typing entirely: you wave to write functions. 💻 This launches while OpenAI faces a hardware-related lawsuit, making the timing anything but accidental. 🧑‍⚖️

If you rely on code sprints, your next project might start with a gesture—and end your relationship with keyboards. 🤔

Could describing a function with hand motions actually save you time, or would it just add friction to your flow?
